tags.name: AI
tags.description: Model-backed decisions about conversations. Bloobability v2 returns, for each policy you write, a calibrated probability that it holds and a separate estimate of whether the conversation can answer it, from the instant or full tier you choose. The deprecated v1 gauge stays documented for reference.

x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.message.reaction: A tapback (classic reaction like `love`/`like` or an emoji) was added to or removed from a message. Payload carries `reaction`, `action` (`add`/`remove`), the reacted `message_id`, `original_text`, the `sender` (the person who reacted — in a group, the member who tapped — or your channel for a reaction you sent; `recipient` is the other side), and — crucially for multi-image sends — `part_index`: WHICH part of a multipart/carousel message was reacted to (0-based, counting the message's parts). The enriched payload also includes the message's full ordered `attachments` array and, when the tapback landed on an image, `reacted_attachment`: the exact `{ index, url, media_type, size, caption }` that was reacted to (null when the reaction targeted a text/caption part or a non-multipart message). So a reaction on the 4th photo of a carousel reports `part_index: 3` and a `reacted_attachment` pointing at that specific image — not just "loved the message". `group` is `{ group_id, name }` in a group chat and `null` in a 1:1 chat. Like the rest of the body, `contact` describes the reacted message: in a group it is the member who wrote that message (`null` when you wrote it), while `sender` is who reacted.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.message.pending: An outbound message row was accepted but no device has taken it yet. Emitted only by the v1/v2 and GHL send paths, which persist the row before dispatching it; a native `/v4` send inserts straight as `queued` and so never reports a pending state. `message.queued` is the first lifecycle event common to every send path.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.safety.state_changed: Fires when a sending number's warm-up tier or safety action changes. Payload carries `tier`, `previous_tier`, `action`, `previous_action` (one of `none`, `queue`, `slow`, `pause_new`, `reply_only`, `review`), and `reasons`.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.safety.number_banned: Fires when Apple bans a dedicated or shared sending number. Payload carries `channel_id`, `phone_number`, `allocation_type` (`dedicated` or `shared`), and `banned_at`.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.number.purchase.completed: A number purchase finished provisioning. Because purchases are asynchronous (the charge triggers a Stripe invoice whose `invoice.paid` provisions the lines), this is how you learn the order succeeded. A purchase may provision several lines, so the payload reports all of them: `purchase_id`, `status` (`completed`), `lines` (one entry per provisioned line, each `{ phone_number, channel_id }`), and the flat `phone_numbers` (E.164) and `channel_ids` (`ch_` ids) arrays covering every provisioned line. When lines are owned by different API keys, every owning key's subscription receives the event.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.number.purchase.action_required: The saved card needs additional authentication (3DS/SCA) before the purchase can complete. Payload carries `purchase_id`, `status` (`action_required`), and `action_url` — open it to finish authentication. Once completed, provisioning proceeds and a `number.purchase.completed` event follows.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.number.purchase.failed: A number purchase failed terminally; no lines were provisioned. Payload carries `purchase_id`, `status` (`failed`), and `reason`.
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.number.removed: A line was removed/unsubscribed (via `DELETE /channels/{channel}` or the dashboard). Payload carries `phone_number`, `channel_id`, `binding_id`, and `reasons` (the churn reason labels).
x-blooio-webhook-event-notes.group.merged: A new group's first message landed in an iMessage conversation another of your groups already holds with the same people on that number, so the new group was folded into it (see Create a group). `group_id` / `chat_id` are the surviving group and its chat; `source_group_id` / `source_chat_id` are the ids returned when the group was created. Also carries `channel_id`, the `message_id` that opened the conversation (now in the surviving chat), and the full surviving `group` object. Replies in that conversation arrive under the survivor.
